name: SpaceX
day_summary: SPCX closed at $174.90 on Day 5 post-IPO (June 18) — down -$16.92 (-8.82%) from the June 17 close of $191.82. The session range was $172.11–$188.41. The $185 daily close stop defined in the entry framework was DECISIVELY TRIGGERED: the close of $174.90 is $10.10 below the stop level, not a marginal breach. This ends the Day 5 'entry framework active' narrative from the morning brief: the framework's own mechanism (stop below $185) requires exiting the position and reassessing at lower levels. The selloff extends the post-IPO two-day decline to -8.3% (Day 4 -5%, Day 5 -8.82% from Day 4 close), bringing SPCX to $2.4T market cap at close (per Bloomberg) — a 22.5% discount from the Day 3 ATH of $225.64. The proximate causes: (1) FOMC hawkish repricing weighing on the highest-multiple name in the US market (94x 2025 revenue); (2) MSCI passive bid deceleration on Day 5 — volume ran well below the Day 3 $324.7M peak, removing the forced-buyer floor; (3) Jim Chanos/ex-Nasdaq-chief short thesis gaining traction as borrow availability improved; (4) lock-up constraints loosening as thin-float mechanics that drove Days 1–3 begin normalizing. The IPO-week rally of +67% from $135 to $225.64 has now partially corrected. The next structured entry requires a stabilization base at $165–$175 and a recovery above $185 on volume before re-engaging the long framework.
long_pnl: IPO allocants from $135 are still +29.6% even at $174.90; FOMC-dip buyers from Day 4 at $187–$192 are 6–9% offside and at-the-stop on the defined-risk structure; the entry-zone framework ($190–$200) never fully executed — the morning brief's 50% sizing at $190–$200 with $185 put hedge was the right structure because the $185 stop capped the loss
short_pnl: best Day 5 payoff in the post-IPO period: -8.82% from $191.82 to $174.90; Jim Chanos and the ex-Nasdaq chief public warnings vindicated near-term; the 'locked-up shares and missing shorts skewed the debut run' thesis is tracking; borrow availability improving means the short book is expanding just as the passive bid exhausts

decision.rationale: STEP ASIDE at HIGH conviction. The $185 daily close stop was triggered at $174.90 — $10.10 below the defined threshold. The framework is unambiguous: exit the position. The Iran blocker is cleared, the entry zone was reached, but the macro regime (FOMC hawkish) overwhelmed the technical support structure. The stop exists to protect against exactly this scenario. Next steps: (1) Exit any SPCX long initiated at the $190–$200 zone; (2) Do NOT re-enter until SPCX shows a two-day close above $185 on above-average volume; (3) Re-assess the entry framework at $165–$175 — if SPCX stabilizes and builds a base for 3–5 sessions, the original $190–$200 entry zone simply resets lower, with a new stop at $165; (4) The June 20 weekly options expiry ($195 max pain) has expired ABOVE current price — the dealer gamma support that was expected on Day 5 did not hold; (5) Monitor the lock-up expiry dynamics (Dec 9, 2026) and first earnings (Sept 2 est.) as the structural re-entry catalysts. Do not add below $185 until two consecutive closes above $185 confirm the stabilization.

The combination of: (1) exhausting passive bid, (2) improving short-borrow availability, (3) FOMC hawkish repricing, and (4) thin Juneteenth-eve tape (no institutional defense) created a perfect bear setup. The $188.41 day high confirms the morning brief's $195 pre-market estimate was wrong — the stock likely opened at or near $185–$188 and sold off from the open.

outlook.short_term: Step aside. The $185 stop was triggered at $174.90 — the framework requires exit. Near-term support at $165–$175 needs to hold for 3–5 sessions to form a base; a recovery above $185 on above-average volume is required before re-engaging. The June 20 weekly options expiry ($195 max pain) removes the current gamma structure and resets to July hedges. The next structured entry is at $165–$175 with a $160 stop, using July puts as the hedge vehicle. Do not catch the falling knife in the $172–$180 zone without a confirmed base.
outlook.long_term: Unchanged. Starlink 5M+ subs (~40% growth), Starship, Starshield, Cursor AI deal (Anysphere $60B stock acquisition confirmed), and the generational infrastructure franchise are intact. The $2.4T market cap at ~84x revenue (at $174.90) remains the valuation overhang but has compressed. First quarterly earnings (~Sept 2) are the fundamental anchor event. December lock-up expiry is the first major supply event. The IPO-week selloff from $225.64 to $174.90 (-22.5%) is a healthy reset of the thin-float mechanics. Patient capital at $165–$175 with a June 20 expiry reset has a better risk/reward than the $190–$200 zone that was invalidated today.

bull_case: IPO allocants from $135 still +29.6% at $174.90 — no structural seller pressure from the original float; the thin-float mechanics (4% public float, $2.4T market cap) mean any new institutional buyer requires the price to rise significantly on available supply; a single large strategic buyer at $165–$175 could catalyze the next leg.

MSCI passive bid is still in the first 2 weeks of its 2–4 week window — the forced buying has not fully exhausted; volume data on June 22 (Monday, post-Juneteenth) will reveal whether the passive bid is still active or has run its course.

Iran ceasefire is in effect — the medium-term macro pathway (Hormuz → oil → CPI → DXY peaks) improves the rate-discount backdrop for high-multiple stocks; SPCX at $165–$175 with the macro improving is a better entry than SPCX at $195–$200 with the macro uncertain.

SpaceX Cursor/Anysphere acquisition at $60B in stock adds an AI software layer — the fundamental franchise is expanding into AI infrastructure; the valuation premium has a new pillar that was not in the IPO prospectus.

Jim Chanos and ex-Nasdaq chief public warnings gaining traction — the 'locked-up shares and missing shorts' thesis means the corrective pressure is structural (borrow improving, MSCI passive bid fading) rather than FOMC-specific; even an FOMC reversal would face this supply headwind.

FOMC hawkish pricing (9/18 dot-plot members projecting hikes) hits 84x-revenue SPCX harder than any other megacap; if Warsh follows through on even one hike, the discount-rate impact on a net-loss company with 0% yield is maximally dilutive.
